CDS-bench: 30-task model pilot

Overview · Four conditions · Additional CoreWeave samples · Model/provider notes · GPT-OSS tools · By task · Settings · Full evaluation

One instance from each of 30 judgment-selected task types, covering translation, RNA, sequence statistics, constrained design, assays and compositions. Each instance is evaluated in easy/hard form, without tools and with offline Python. Two identical hard variants are omitted, leaving 30 easy and 28 hard prompts, or 116 attempts per complete model. This is a small model/provider comparison, not a representative estimate over the full benchmark. Full-evaluation requests are separate.

All failures remain in the denominator. An asterisk marks a stopped run, whose completed subset is not directly comparable to a complete run. Times are complete-example medians, including failures and tool round trips. Token budgets include reasoning and all tool turns.

Recorded cost covers only the retained completed attempts. Compatibility checks, interrupted requests, discarded duplicate-hard cases and GPT-OSS follow-ups are excluded. Missing billing records are not assumed to be zero. OpenRouter pilot requests had a 300-second deadline. Both internal Marin checkpoints use a 1,800-second request deadline: Snowball RC (2026.09.21) has a 16,384-token aggregate budget and Snowball v0.1 has 32,768 tokens. Both are mixture-of-experts models with 67B total parameters and 2B active per token. RC means release candidate. Neither API exposes per-request pricing. Unavailable cost is not zero.

Models are ordered by mean task accuracy over their completed cases, giving each available task equal weight. Partial runs cover different subsets, so this display order is not a matched model ranking.

Public request, reasoning and tool traces include the saved pilots, follow-up checks, interrupted attempts and provider diagnostics. Credentials and private endpoints are redacted.

Model/provider notes

GPT-6 Luna (high) · openai

Completed all four conditions. This is the original pilot, restricted to the same 116 retained cases; the historical responses are unchanged.

openai/gpt-6-luna; reasoning {"effort":"high","exclude":false}; no provider fallback.

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 · morph/fp8

Stopped to switch models after the complete easy/no-tools, hard/no-tools and easy/Python passes, plus 13 hard/Python attempts. The partial hard/Python subset should not be treated as a full-pass score.

deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017; reasoning {"effort":"high","exclude":false}; no provider fallback.

Beam 1.0 501B A23B · nebius/fp4

Completed all four conditions. 43 of 118 attempted Python calls failed in the retained cases. Returned programs sometimes contained trailing PY delimiters, XML argument tags or stray quotes. Programs were executed verbatim. The pilot does not separate model behavior from provider parsing. All six answer-format failures become exact matches under the separate formatting diagnostic.

reflection/beam-1.0-501b-a23b; reasoning {"effort":"high","exclude":false}; no provider fallback.

Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B A55B · nvidia

Stopped at the user’s request because the free endpoint was too slow. The first three passes completed; only 12 hard/Python attempts finished. Free-endpoint pacing contributes to example time.

nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free; reasoning {"effort":"high","exclude":false}; no provider fallback.

Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (CoreWeave) · coreweave/bf16

Completed all 116 attempts: 45 correct (38.8%). No API/protocol errors or request timeouts; 35 token caps, all without tools. Python improved the score from 11/58 without tools to 34/58 with tools. All 169 calls had valid function names and JSON arguments; 136 executions succeeded and 33 had program errors. A separate fresh run of the same Lightning model on CoreWeave BF16 only, with no fallback. Uses the same retained prompts, reasoning enabled, omitted seed, 32,768-token aggregate budget, 300-second request deadline, collector, original JSON Python function and offline sandbox as the io.net run. Seed remains omitted to hold it fixed across providers, although CoreWeave advertises seed support. Starts with ten concurrent examples and no pacing. io.net results are retained separately and are not pooled with this run.

nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning; reasoning {"enabled":true,"exclude":false}; no provider fallback.

Qwen 3.7 Flash (high) · alibaba/us-east-1

Completed all four conditions. Python improved scores and reduced example time, but many final answers still violated the required format. Formatting-only recoveries are reported separately; primary scores are unchanged. The later full evaluation uses fresh requests, not these responses.

qwen/qwen3.7-flash; reasoning {"effort":"high","exclude":false}; no provider fallback.

North Mini Code · cohere

Stopped at the user’s request because it was too slow. All 30 easy/no-tools cases and only three hard/no-tools cases finished. No scored Python condition was reached; its tool preflight succeeded separately. It exposes reasoning enable/disable, not an effort-level selector.

cohere/north-mini-code:free; reasoning {"enabled":true,"exclude":false}; no provider fallback.

GPT-OSS 20B · amazon-bedrock

Completed on Amazon Bedrock, with 24 tool-protocol/API failures: 19 HTTP 400 tool-message rejections and five failures from continued calls after the eight-call limit. Some function names contained Harmony channel markup; other calls contained invalid JSON arguments. The initial preflight passed, but scored tool cases were unreliable. See the separate provider diagnostics below.

openai/gpt-oss-20b; reasoning {"effort":"high","exclude":false}; no provider fallback.

Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (io.net) · io-net

Stopped at the user’s request because it was too slow. 81/116 attempts finished, with 21 correct (25.9%), a 154.7-second median and $0.12087 in recorded charges. Failures: 6 incorrect values, 8 formatting failures, 25 timeouts, 2 token caps and 19 API/protocol errors. 3 interrupted attempts are preserved but excluded from scoring and timing. The hard/Python pass was not reached. Uses io.net only, with no provider fallback. Reasoning is enabled without an advertised effort selector; seed is omitted because io.net does not advertise support. Quantization is undisclosed. The same 32,768-token aggregate budget, 300-second request deadline, original JSON Python function and offline sandbox apply. The collector also detects nested streaming provider errors and preserves raw reasoning strings when structured reasoning details are absent; no answer or tool-program repair is applied. Repeated provider errors stopped the initial run after 56 attempts. Only unissued cases then continued with 3 concurrent examples and 5-second request spacing. All initial failures remain unchanged; no scored request was retried. Stopped at user request because io.net was too slow; switching to a separate CoreWeave run. Completed results retained; interrupted requests excluded from scoring and timing.

nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning; reasoning {"enabled":true,"exclude":false}; no provider fallback.

Snowball v0.1 · Marin internal API

Uses the newer Marin-Snowball-67B-A2B-v0.1 checkpoint on the existing internal Marin/vLLM BF16 service. The same native Delphi transport, exact Python function and offline sandbox apply, with thinking enabled, temperature 0.7, seed 20261029 and concurrency 60. This pilot restores the 32,768-token aggregate budget while retaining the 1,800-second API deadline. The older Snowball RC (2026.09.21) used 16,384 tokens, so this comparison changes both checkpoint and output budget. No effort-level selector is verified. The unscored preflight executed Python and returned its correct result, but appended a stray Markdown fence; its strict formatting failure is preserved. The actual execution and returned-result delivery were verified separately without retrying or repairing that answer. Primary pilot scoring is unchanged. Costs and reasoning-only token counts are unavailable.

open-athena/Marin-Snowball-67B-A2B-v0.1; reasoning {"enabled":true,"effort":null,"mechanism":"chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=true"}; no provider fallback.

Gemma 4 31B · novita/bf16

Stopped because it was too slow/flaky, after 24 easy/no-tools cases. No hard or scored Python condition was reached. The earlier Crusoe preflight was rate-limited; scored requests used Novita BF16.

google/gemma-4-31b-it; reasoning {"enabled":true,"exclude":false}; no provider fallback.

Snowball RC (2026.09.21) · Marin internal API

Snowball RC (2026.09.21), the older release candidate, uses the internal Marin/vLLM BF16 service rather than OpenRouter. Its Delphi chat template enables thinking; there is no verified high-effort selector. The server lacks automatic function parsing, so the client supplies the unchanged Python function via the native xml_tools template argument, parses only complete JSON tool_call blocks, and stops generation at the closing tool-call tag. Native thinking is preserved and replayed. Generated Python and final answers are not repaired. A real two-request sandboxed Python round trip passed before scoring. At the user’s request, this model uses a 16,384-token aggregate budget and 1,800-second API deadline. The eight-call limit and offline Python/NumPy environment are unchanged. The earlier 32,768-token/300-second trial is preserved separately and is excluded from these scores. Temperature is explicitly 0.7, seed 20261029; sixty examples run concurrently across all four conditions. API usage reports tokens but no monetary charges, so cost is unavailable rather than zero.

open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21; reasoning {"enabled":true,"effort":null,"mechanism":"chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=true"}; no provider fallback.

Snowball RC (2026.09.21) provenance: Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21, open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21 at revision b8c07f7df1df65525abbfdbcd1572318ba11c42f. Pilot audit.

Tool verification: 195 successful Python executions, 32 program failures and 16 rejected calls. 3 attempts returned malformed native tool JSON or tags; 7 continued calling after the limit. These remain failed attempts. Scored HTTP failures: 0.

LFM 2.5 24B A2B · liquid/fp8

Completed all four conditions using the approved 8,192-token aggregate budget, the endpoint’s output limit, rather than 32,768. Reasoning was enabled without an effort selector. Ninety-nine attempts exhausted that budget. All 55 emitted tool calls had valid names and JSON arguments; 47 executions succeeded and eight had program errors, mostly undefined variables in a fresh interpreter. This does not establish performance at a larger budget.

liquid/lfm-2.5-24b-a2b; reasoning {"enabled":true,"exclude":false}; no provider fallback.

GPT-OSS: no reliable OpenRouter tool setup established

On ten matched easy instances, CoreWeave with a renamed JSON function improved from 3/10 without tools to 5/10 with tools, but four tool attempts failed at the protocol level. The local sandbox successfully executed many valid programs. These exploratory checks used subsets selected partly for earlier failures, so they are not independent model accuracy estimates and are not pooled into the pilot table.

Variants tried renaming the function, accepting raw Python arguments without repairing code, explicit fresh-script/print instructions, non-streaming requests, lower temperature, a forced first tool call, hidden returned reasoning, high/medium effort, and Groq/DeepInfra endpoints. DeepInfra was rate-limited and was not substantively evaluated. Responses API checks also failed. No hosted interpreter or web tool was enabled.

A native Harmony harness is a documented candidate, not a locally verified fix. The tested OpenRouter configurations do not establish a general limit on GPT-OSS tool capability.

Settings, execution and saved data

High reasoning was requested where supported. Gemma, North, Liquid and Nemotron Lightning expose reasoning enable/disable without an effort selector. OpenRouter pilot calls used provider-default temperature, a seed where supported (omitted on Bedrock and both Lightning runs), streaming responses and initially ten concurrent examples. North and Nemotron Ultra starts were paced for free-endpoint limits. After provider errors, io.net continued only unissued cases at concurrency three with five-second request spacing; its timing includes that scheduling change.

Both Snowball models have 67B total parameters and 2B active per token. They use native thinking and tool-call transport, temperature 0.7, seed 20261029 and concurrency 60; their checkpoint provenance, budgets and transport differences are recorded above. Python 3.12.9 + NumPy 2.5.4, no Biopython. The custom function runs locally under /usr/bin/sandbox-exec, with networking and process forks denied, and restricted file access. Each call starts a fresh interpreter; files persist within the example. Limits: eight Python calls/example, 30 seconds/call, 16,384 characters each of stdout/stderr. The no-tools condition supplies no functions. Web plugins are disabled. Network denial is an executor policy, not an OpenRouter parameter.
